column7: Claims a row's upstream cancel with the caller's or the parked offer and parks an unusable offer on a still-working row; a mistake loses the owner's cancel or claims twice (MIK-8347).
Decides whether a pending cancel is sent now, waits for its back-off, or is given up by age or an unresolvable backend, and records the outcome; a mistake resends after the bound or never sends.
Holds the row lock through claim, send and outcome, then re-claims while the row's generation moved; the r3.4 lost-cancel window lives here.
First-sender entry: an owner's Detach never queues on the row lock and claims inline before spawning the send; a worker's Inline waits; a mistake makes the owner wait on the peer or loses the claim.
Gets or creates the row entry and bumps its generation before any lock attempt, the ordering the re-check relies on.
Drops an idle entry only under the map lock with no holder and no parked offer, so a sender never gets a second mutex for one row.
Drops a deleted row's entry and parked offer unless a sender still holds it.
Selects due or started-backend pending rows and spawns a retry for each row whose lock is free; never awaits a send.
Installs the recovery adapter once and starts listening to its backend-start feed.
Retries a started backend's pending cancels on each start, all of them after a lag; holds only a weak executor reference.

The durable pending-cancel shape shared by the claim and the preflight reservation: target index where a target names the backend, a copy only otherwise; a mistake overflows the record budget or misdirects the cancel.

Writes an attempt's outcome: confirmed or a bound reached clears pending and marks sent in one write; failed sends count, not-ready ones do not; a mistake resends a confirmed cancel or retries forever.
The widest encoding of a pending claim the dispatch preflight reserves.
Lists pending rows due by back-off or age, or those of one backend.
Whether a pending cancel passed its 24-hour cap.
Resolves the backend a pending cancel goes to through its target index or its copied name; a mistake sends the cancel to the wrong backend or none.
